Agenda item 4.03, Indigenous People's Day and Native American Heritage Month proclamation. I call on Miss Lady for a proclamation. Whereas Indigenous People's Day is recognized on the second Monday of October, and Native American Heritage Month is recognized throughout the month of November across the United States and in Fairfax County Public Schools to honor and celebrate the history, accomplishments, and contributions of the first peoples of this land.

And whereas in 1990, Congress passed and President George H.W. Bush signed into law a joint resolution designating the month of November as the first National American Indian Heritage Month, in 2021, President Joe Biden was the first U.S. President to formally commemorate Indigenous Peoples Day as a national holiday with a presidential proclamation.

And whereas Indigenous people have made invaluable contributions in the sciences, arts, public service, military service, and many other fields that are integral to the advancement of our nation and society. And whereas the Commonwealth of Virginia is home to 11 officially recognized tribes whose presence and leadership honors and strengthens our shared history and future.

And whereas Fairfax County sits on the land originally stewarded by the Doge, Manahoic, and Pomonkey tribes and other indigenous peoples whose stories, traditions, and cultures continue to enrich our country and commonwealth. And whereas FCPS serves a diverse student population with many who embrace and celebrate their indigenous family heritage.

Whereas Indigenous Peoples Day and Native American Heritage Month are wonderful opportunities for our Fairfax County Public Schools community to honor our nation's original inhabitants and their descendants. These commemorations further call us to honor the beautiful and rich indigenous communities, traditions, cultures, and lives across our county, commonwealth, and all around the world.

Now therefore be it resolved that the Fairfax County School Board does hereby proclaim October 13, 2025 as Indigenous Peoples Day and November 2025 as Native American Heritage Month in recognition and celebration of the many contributions of our nation's indigenous people to our school system, community, and country.

WAVES allowed over 80,000 women to serve in new and crucial roles, such as aeronautical engineers, parachute riggers, and cryptographers.
